newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO prices rangebound in dull market.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO prices rangebound in dull market.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices are expected to remain rangebound due to lacklustre talks, traders said on Wednesday.
"I do not expect any big changes," said a Singapore-based trader. "Fundamentals have been like this for some time," added.

Major regional buyers of spot cargoes such as China have either stayed away from the market or bid at very low prices of $108-$109 per tonne for September delivery cargoes of 180 cst on a cost-and-freight basis.
Traders expected prices to remain at around the $104.00 per tonne mark for fob Singapore 180 cst cargoes for September loading.
One trader from a major oil company said it was prepared to bid $104.50 for a 20,000 tonne 180 cst cargo. Traders said they expected a western trader to support the 380 cst price and bid for cargoes.
But some sources said aggressive sellers of South Korean cargoes of high sulphur fuel oil has prompted market rumours of problems in South Korea's refining industry.
Singapore September paper was quoted at $104.50-$105.25, little changed from Tuesday's indications with no trade reported.
